speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have been experiencing chronic pain in your left shoulder without any history of trauma. To help me pinpoint the cause, have you noticed if the pain worsens when you raise your arm overhead, or does it hurt more when you reach behind your back?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old woman. The patient reports a 2-month history of insidious onset left shoulder pain, worsening with extreme ranges of motion and activity. Pain disrupts sleep, and there's noted difficulty with activities of daily living like brushing hair and dressing. No history of shoulder trauma, neck pain, arm/hand weakness, numbness, or paresthesias. The patient has type 2 diabetes mellitus, treated with metformin and glipizide.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Rotator Cuff Tear (likely Supraspinatus).

The combination of chronic pain, specific weakness in overhead activities, and significant difficulty with daily tasks like combing hair is highly suggestive of a rotator cuff tear. Given your age and diabetes, a complete tear is possible. Have you noticed any specific weakness lifting your arm to the side, or has it become difficult to lift it at all? REQUEST IMAGES: Shoulder_Xray, Shoulder_MRI
